resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Foundation dates the first light to 1849; the record's 1848 is the year the brick tower was finished.
The 1859 date is when Congress voted money and construction began; the cast-iron tower was not completed until 1868.

The Foundation gives 25 July 1894 for the relighting; the 1894 Board report gives 26 July as the planned date for showing the new light; the 1895 Board list gives 25 July as the date the light was moved. The story states all three.
The Foundation's history gives a mile and a quarter inland; its fact sheet gives a mile. The story gives both.
The Foundation says nine head keepers in 155 years; the archive roster lists fourteen principal-keeper entries and twelve different men. Not resolved; the story states both.

notes_for_editor: (1) The Foundation says the last keeper left in 1941, but the archive roster lists principal keepers into the 1950s (Carr from 1952, Swain to 1952) and the record gives automation as 1954. Not resolved. (2) Head keepers: the Foundation says nine; the roster has twelve different principal keepers. Not resolved. (3) Scobie: roster 1848-1850, Foundation says he abandoned the light in 1849. Story uses the Foundation's account. (4) The relight date: LHB 1894 report says the temporary light was discontinued on 26 July 1894; the 1895 list says the move was 25 July 1894. Story gives both. (5) The Civil War account (lamps removed and buried, lights ordered dark) rests on the Foundation alone. A Chronicling America search for Canaveral and Burnham in Florida papers, 1853-1876, returned no hits. The Wikipedia lead gives the same story but is not cited. (6) Women keepers: the Foundation has a 'Women Who Kept the Lights' page; the PDF returned no text, so it was not read, and the roster marks no keeper as a woman. Recheck this page if a woman's service is confirmed. (7) The Foundation's fact sheet says 'Repeated flooding from 1971' (likely a typo for 1871); the story does not use the date of the flooding. (8) The record gives 'ownership: nonprofit'; the Foundation says the Air Force (2000) and the Space Force (2020) own the tower. Proposed correction. (9) The record's 1868 light is a first-order Fresnel lens; the Foundation dates the lens to 1868 to 1993. Consistent. (10) Character of the 1893 storm: the Board's account uses 'the cyclone' and 'the storm' for 27-28 August 1893; the story follows the report. (11) Wikipedia lead used for orientation only. Quotes are from the Foundation (paraphrased), the Board's reports (public domain), the Bulletin and the Commissioner's report. (12) Visiting: the Foundation provides tours; the tower sits on Space Force property; the story says to arrange access in advance. | CHECK 2026-10-27: the record's 1954 automation date is not in the USLHS place record or in the Foundation pages read; the story no longer gives it. The Foundation's fact sheet says 'Repeated flooding from 1971'; the story does not use a flooding date. Visiting: the Foundation runs tours and group requests; the tower is on Space Force property; the story says to arrange visits through the Foundation and not to go onto base ground.
